title: Busymail - AI email client that surfaces what needs you
excerpt: Busymail connects to your Gmail, Yahoo, or another mail server it can reach, reads it with AI, and surfaces what needs you: the reply, the bill, the flight. $15 a month plus tax, with a 14-day refund on your first payment.
content_html:
An email client that reads your inbox - and lets your AI work in it.

Busymail connects to your Gmail, Yahoo, or any IMAP server Busymail can reach, and surfaces the few things that need you - the reply, the bill, the flight. Give an AI client a token and it can work the same mailbox: read it, tidy it, draft mail. Nothing it writes sends until you approve it.

about two minutes to set up

Prefer a desktop app? Download for macOS, Windows, or Linux

The macOS build is for Apple Silicon Macs; there is no Intel build. The desktop builds aren't code-signed yet, so macOS and Windows warn you when you open the app. The download page walks through the steps. Signed and notarized builds are coming.

On a phone? Download the Android app

Android warns about installing from an unknown source. Allow it for whichever app does the download.

You read your mail

Grouped by what it is, with the dates, amounts and actions pulled out of the mail.

Your AI drafts, and waits

It drafts the message; the send waits here until you approve it, with every recipient and attachment spelled out.

Pricing

One price. Every mailbox you connect.

14-day refund on your first payment, no questions asked.
Plus VAT or sales tax where it applies.

Your inbox

Your mail, grouped by what it is

Busymail sorts every message into groups - finance, travel, code, security, personal and the rest - and pulls the dates, amounts and actions out of the mail, so you can see what a thread wants without opening it. Nothing is deleted and nothing is hidden. When something changes, it comes back up.

Search, pins, an archive that really archives, and apps for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android.

AI access

Let Claude, or any MCP client, work in your mail

Once you have an account, you create a token in Settings and point an AI client at your mailbox. You choose what it may do, and you can revoke it in one click. It is not a mailbox you move to - you keep your accounts where they are.

Read your mail

Your feed, any conversation in full, your sent mail, what is inside a file attached to it, and search across all of it.

Tidy it up

Archive, unarchive, pin and unpin. Archiving really moves the mail out of your inbox on your mail server, so it changes what you see in every other mail app too.

Draft mail

A reply, or a new message to anyone. It writes, and the message waits for you. It can attach files too.

No token can change your settings, your password or your two-factor, add or remove an email account, or create and revoke tokens. Those stay with you. How to connect a client →

Approvals

Nothing it writes gets sent without you

A token can never send mail. When an assistant writes a message, it waits under Approvals until you approve or reject it - the recipients, the subject, the body, and every attachment named and sized. Approving happens while you are signed in, so the token that wrote a message cannot approve it.

An address you have never corresponded with

It gets flagged, Approve stops being the filled button, and Reject takes the warning outline. The domain of every recipient is spelled out, because that is the part the eye skips.

You hear about it

The queue updates itself without a refresh, and the notifications that tell you about new mail tell you an approval is waiting too.

Undecided is not sent

A message nobody decides on is discarded after a week, and nothing reaches the recipients in the meantime.

Getting started

Works with your Gmail, Yahoo, or any IMAP server Busymail can reach

1

Connect your inbox

Add your email with an app password. Gmail and Yahoo have step-by-step instructions, and any other provider works when its mail server is on the public internet, reachable over TLS on port 993, and still issues app passwords. A server on port 143, one only reachable on your own network, or a provider that has closed the password path cannot be added. Google only creates an app password once 2-Step Verification is on, and the form walks you through turning it on first.Microsoft 365 and Outlook accounts cannot be connected: they need an OAuth sign-in Busymail does not have.

2

Busymail reads the signal

An AI pulls out the dates, amounts, and actions hiding in your mail. Reading changes nothing - your mail stays exactly where it is.

3

See what matters

Grouped, ranked, and quietly resurfaced when things change. Nothing is deleted, nothing hidden.

Private by design

You're handing Busymail your inbox.

So here's the deal, plainly.

✓

Your credentials are encrypted, and your data is stored in the EU (Amsterdam).

✓

Busymail never sells your data, and never uses it to train AI.

✓

To find signals, your email is processed by a third-party AI under zero data retention - never stored there, never used to train models. Read the details.

✓

Give an AI client a token and it can read your mail - your feed, conversations and searches. Only if you choose to, and only until you revoke it.

✓

You can let it tidy up too, and archiving really moves the mail - out of your inbox into your archive folder on your own mail server, so it changes what you see in Apple Mail as well.

✓

You can let it draft mail too, and it still cannot send - anything it writes waits for you to approve or reject it here first.

✓

Revoke access whenever you like, in one click.

See just the signal.

$15 a month, plus VAT or sales tax where it applies. If it turns out not to be for you, ask within 14 days of your first payment and you get it back, no questions asked.
